name: 东北话 (Northeastern Mandarin)
summary: 东北官话 is the Mandarin variety of Heilongjiang, Jilin and most of Liaoning. Round 2 dropped rare or dated items (老蒯, 马胡陆, 卜留克, 便所, 味素, 冰果, 列巴, 抠搜) and rebuilt vocabulary from Wiktionary entries and a 2015 feature article with example sentences (The World of Chinese), plus the Chinese Wikipedia phonology section used as a pointer (it still has many uncited statements). No verified Northeastern final-particle system was found, so the particle list is short and honest. Confidence is better for words and set phrases than for grammar or sound details.

grammar.condition: 整 stands in for do, get, make, fix, handle. Wiktionary lists the sense with example 這可咋整啊 (Northeastern) and 整幾個小菜 (to fix a few side dishes). The World of Chinese says its range is 'almost indefinable' and gives 给我整两瓶啤酒.
grammar.romanization: gěi wǒ zhěng liǎng píng píjiǔ

grammar.condition: 咋 'how/why' + 整. Source examples: 空调坏了，咋整？ and 這可咋整啊？

grammar.standard: 怎么了 / 什么事 (what is going on?)
grammar.condition: zh.wikipedia lists 咋地 as 'how come / what's the matter' within the 咋 group. The page has no citation for it. Also used as the retort in 瞅你咋地 (source 3).
Question word in Northeastern Mandarin (Harbin, Shenyang, Qiqihar listed by Wiktionary), also in Jilu and Central Plains Mandarin, so it is not uniquely Northeastern. zh.wikipedia lists 啥前儿 (when).

grammar.standard: 干什么 (what are you doing / where are you off to?)
grammar.dialect: 嘎哈 (also written 干哈 / 噶哈)
grammar.condition: Source 3 uses 嘎哈 as '干啥' in the greeting 你嘎哈去？ and says to stretch the 'há' and open the vowel. zh.wikipedia writes 噶哈呢 and says it comes from 干啥呢. Written forms vary: choose one and keep it.

grammar.standard: 很 / 特别 (intensifier before an adjective)
grammar.condition: Wiktionary lists 贼 'very' as originally dialectal, including Northeastern Mandarin, now increasingly colloquial. Source 3 gives 这馆子贼啦好吃. Heavy use sounds like a caricature.

grammar.standard: 很 / 特别 ... 了 (emotional intensifier)
grammar.condition: Rui et al. 2023 compare 老 and 超 as degree adverbs and say both express strong subjective attitude and emotion. The pattern 老A了 is also named in search snippets I did not open. Treat this example as constructed.
grammar.romanization: zhè ge cài lǎo hǎochī le

grammar.condition: Source 3: 你瞅啥 is a challenge that assumes the other person's look was provocative; replying 瞅你咋地 escalates. Use only for tension scenes.
grammar.romanization: nǐ chǒu shá? / chǒu nǐ zǎ dì?

grammar.standard: verb reduplication for a casual chat invitation
grammar.condition: Source 3 gives 咱俩唠唠 ('let's have a word') and says it can be the opening of a fight. Verb reduplication 唠唠 softens the verb in Mandarin too. 咱 = inclusive 'we'.
Source 3: 彪 (biāo) and 虎 (hǔ) mean foolish, reckless. Example: 坐火车忘了带身份证？你彪啊！ A mild insult among friends, rude in anger.

vocabulary.note: Common across Northern Mandarin; in the Northeast it is the everyday 'what'.
How/why. Wiktionary page does not label it Northeastern, but zh.wikipedia and source 3 use 咋整 / 咋地.
Set phrase 'what do we do'. Very recognizable.
Greeting or question 'doing what'. Varied spelling: 嘎哈 / 干哈 / 噶哈.
All-purpose verb, see grammar.
Intensifier. Originally 'thief'. Write 贼啦 only for emphasis.
Wiktionary's synonym table lists 嘎嘎 for 'very' in Harbin; usage today (e.g. 嘎嘎新) is slangy and young.
Dirty, grubby. Also a verb 'mock, speak ill of'. Wiktionary lists it for Harbin.
Ugly or shabby; mainly Northeastern colloquial. Source 3: 你写的字太磕碜了吧.
Chat. Wiktionary lists the erhua form 嘮嗑兒 for Northeastern cities (Shenyang, Changchun, Harbin).
Show off, swagger, and also squander money. Source 3 example about spending a whole paycheck. Teasing tone.
Colloquial 'look'. 你瞅啥 is a famous challenge.
Colloquial 'trick, sweet-talk'. Originally Northeastern; spread nationally through Zhao Benshan sketches (so it no longer marks region). 大忽悠 = con man.
Wiktionary: 'be fond of' in northern colloquial speech; also 'to care about' (usually negative). Not Northeast-only.
Annoy, nauseate, feel disgusted. Mainly northern dialect. Variants 硌硬, 咯应.
Talk nonsense. Wiktionary lists it for Harbin and does not mark it vulgar, but it is rude in tone. Use among friends or in conflict.
Corner or remote place; 犄角旮旯 = every nook. Wiktionary calls it dialectal. 这旮旯 (this place) was not found on that page.
Foolish or reckless. Insult among friends, hostile in anger.
zh.wikipedia: to lie, or to talk endlessly. Uncited.
zh.wikipedia lists it as an example of 啥. Uncited and uncertain: have a native confirm.
Corn. Wiktionary has 苞米 as a variant of 包米 with no dialect label; zh.wikipedia lists it uncited. Widely known as a Northeastern word, but only weakly verified here.

particles.function: Softens an exclamation or insult. Example from source 3: 你彪啊！ Same particle as Mandarin 啊.
Suggestion or mild doubt, as in Mandarin. Source 3: 你写的字太磕碜了吧.
Progressive or question tag. zh.wikipedia lists 噶哈呢 (from 干啥呢) 'what are you doing'.

pronunciation.rule: The r- initial is largely lost. zh.wikipedia lists 肉 yòu, 柔 yóu, 人 yín, 软 yuǎn (zero or y- initial), and in a few words l-: 如 lú, 瑞 luì. English Wikipedia says r- is 'generally elided'. The Chinese page says older speakers in eastern Jilin pronounce r as y, but younger speakers drift towards Standard Mandarin. These statements carry no citation.
pronunciation.actor_tip: For 人, 肉, 日, 软 use a light y- start (or no consonant). Use it on a few high-frequency words, not on every r. A younger character should use it less.
pronunciation.example: 肉 ròu → yòu; 人 rén → yín

pronunciation.rule: -ian and -üan have a more open vowel, [æ] rather than [ɛ] or [e] (cited to Li Wen-Chao 2004 on the Chinese page).
pronunciation.actor_tip: Open the jaw on 天, 先, 点, 元: sounds like 'tæn' with a wide 'a'.

pronunciation.rule: After b/p/m/f the vowel o is read as [ɤ] (like Korean 어), cited to 中国语言地图集.
pronunciation.actor_tip: Say bo, po, mo, fo as 'buh, puh, muh, fuh' with 어-like vowel.

pronunciation.rule: w- is kept as w (not v as in some Hebei speech). English Wikipedia.
pronunciation.actor_tip: Keep a clean w on 我, 为, 王.

pronunciation.rule: zh/ch/sh and z/c/s mix depending on sub-area (uncited on zh.wikipedia): Meixi sub-group reads them all flat, 肇扶 sub-group all retroflex, 蛟宁 sub-group varies freely.
pronunciation.actor_tip: Do not make a Northeastern character say all-flat zh/ch/sh unless the setting is Shenyang-Fushun-type speech. Standard retroflex sounds are safe for most Harbin-type speakers.
pronunciation.example: 知道 zhīdào (flat or retroflex by area)

pronunciation.rule: Zero-initial syllables get an n- start in the Ha-Fu group (Harbin, Fuxin, Changchun area), e.g. 摁 nèn, 矮 nǎi, 鹅 né (uncited).
pronunciation.actor_tip: Optional colour for a Harbin or Changchun character: add a light n- before 阿, 爱, 安, 鹅 words. Skip it for Shenyang.
pronunciation.example: 矮 ǎi → nǎi; 鹅 é → né

pronunciation.rule: Erhua is more frequent than in Beijing; the page's example is 超市 → 超市儿 in the Shenyang area. The citation is a WeChat article, so evidence is weak.
pronunciation.actor_tip: Add a light -r to small nouns and set phrases (唠嗑儿, 一会儿). Do not r-ify every noun.

pronunciation.rule: No -m final (原文 无-m尾韵), cited to 汉语方言学基础教程 p.125. The Northeast has no final -m, but Standard Mandarin has none either, so this changes nothing for a Mandarin-based script.

tones_intonation.rule: Old entering-tone (clipped) syllables spread over all four tones (1, 2, 3, 4), with rules that are not very regular, much like Beijing. A higher share of voiceless-initial entering syllables go to tone 3 than in Beijing (cited to 汉语方言学基础教程 p.140).
Yin-ping (tone 1) is slightly lower than Beijing's 55: 44 or 33 (zh.wikipedia, uncited).
Distance from Beijing speech: Harbin is closer than Jilin and Changchun, and these are closer than Shenyang (English Wikipedia). So Harbin-style speech is the safest 'neutral Dongbei' base.
Source 3's practical advice: stretch 'há' in 嘎哈 and open the vowel wider than in Standard Mandarin. In confrontation lines like 你瞅啥 the delivery is a challenge, not a question.

examples.note: 원문 예문. há를 길게 끌고 입을 크게 벌리는 느낌으로.

examples.romanization: gěi wǒ zhěng liǎng píng píjiǔ
examples.note: 원문 예문. 整는 '가져오다/만들다'까지 두루 쓰는 만능 동사.
원문 예문. 贼啦는 강조. 대사 한 줄에 한 번만.
시비를 거는 대표 문장. 질문이 아니라 도전하는 억양.

examples.note: 원문 예문. 彪 = 바보 같다. 친구 사이의 가벼운 욕.
원문에서 시비의 신호로도 쓰인다고 한 표현. 장면에 따라 다정할 수도, 위협일 수도.

examples.romanization: nǐ xiě de zì tài kēchen le ba
examples.note: 원문 예문. 磕碜 = 보기 흉하다.

examples.korean_idea: 월급 받은 지 이틀 만에 다 써 버렸네.(놀림)
examples.putonghua: 刚发的工资，没两天就被你花光了。
examples.regional: 刚发的工资，没两天就被你嘚瑟光了。
examples.romanization: gāng fā de gōngzī, méi liǎng tiān jiù bèi nǐ dèse guāng le
examples.note: 원문 예문. 嘚瑟 = 으스대며 돈 쓰다.

examples.korean_idea: 이 일 진짜 어떡하지, 걱정돼.(위로가 필요한 사람에게)
examples.note: Wiktionary 예문(동북 표시). 위로 장면에서 상대의 걱정을 받아 주는 대사로 쓸 수 있음.

examples.romanization: zhè ge cài lǎo hǎochī le
examples.note: 老A了는 주관적 감정을 강하게 표현한다는 연구 요약에 근거한 조합. 원어민 확인 필요.
扯犊子 = 헛소리. 거친 톤이라 친구 사이나 싸움에서만.

sub_regions.region: 吉沈片 (Jishen; Shenyang, Fushun, Benxi, Anshan; Jilin, Yanbian)
sub_regions.features: Zero-initial syllables stay zero-initial (52 counties/cities per zh.wikipedia). Meixi sub-group reads zh/ch/sh flat. Further from Beijing speech than Harbin or Changchun (English Wikipedia).

sub_regions.region: 哈阜片 (Ha-Fu; Harbin, Changchun, Songyuan, Fuxin, Jinzhou)
sub_regions.features: Zero-initial syllables get n- (67 counties/cities); Zhaofu sub-group reads zh/ch/sh retroflex. Harbin speech is the closest to Beijing Mandarin. A safe default for a generic 'Dongbei' character.

sub_regions.region: 黑松片 (Heisong; Qiqihar, Heihe, Daqing, Yichun, Jiamusi)
sub_regions.features: Zero-initial syllables are mixed: some zero, some ng-/n- (the zh.wikipedia statement carries 'needs explanation'). Northern Heilongjiang and Inner Mongolia border.
No source I opened compares Heilongjiang, Jilin and Liaoning speech at the province level. The sub-group names above are the only verified split, and they cut across provinces.

common_mistakes: Packing 嘎哈, 整, 贼, 唠嗑儿, 扯犊子 into every line. This is the classic caricature. Roughly one regional item per sentence at most, in casual speech only.
Turning every r into y. It is a few words (人, 肉, 软), weaker in younger speakers.
Using 你瞅啥 and 瞅你咋地 as everyday talk. They are fighting words.
Writing 老蒯, 马胡陆, 卜留克 or other dated or rare words. They are removed on purpose.
Treating 稀罕, 膈应, 忽悠 or 啥 as only Northeastern. They are used in much of northern China, and 忽悠 became national slang.
Using Dongbei words in formal speech, narration or announcements.
Inventing final particles (呗, 昂, 嗷, 哈). No opened source confirmed them.
generational_notes: zh.wikipedia says older speakers in eastern Jilin pronounce r as y, and younger speakers are moving towards Standard Mandarin (uncited).
忽悠 spread nationally via Zhao Benshan sketches (Wiktionary, source 3), so younger people may not hear it as Northeastern.
嘎嘎 as an intensifier (Harbin per Wiktionary) is slangy; its age profile was not verified.
conversion_guidelines: Write natural spoken Mandarin first, in film-dialogue register. Then add at most 1 or 2 regional items per sentence from the verified list: 啥, 咋, 咋整, 嘎哈, 整, 贼, 埋汰, 磕碜, 唠嗑儿, 嘚瑟, 瞅, 忽悠, 扯犊子, 旮旯.
Keep Mandarin sentence structure. The only verified structures are 整 as a general verb, 咋 + verb questions, 贼/老 + adjective, 你嘎哈去, and 咱俩唠唠. Do not invent others.
Add erhua lightly, on small nouns, not everywhere. Use 咱 for inclusive 'we' when the characters are friends.
Do not add the final particles 呗, 昂, 嗷, 哈 until a source is found.
For a neutral Dongbei character use Harbin-type speech (closest to Beijing). Add Jishen or Heisong details only when the setting is named.
Make insults and fighting lines (你彪啊, 扯犊子, 你瞅啥) clearly flagged for director approval.
Mark each constructed line as constructed and ask a Northeastern native to rate how natural it sounds before performance.

open_questions: Verified Northeastern final particles (呗, 昂, 嗷, 嚎, 哈, 哩) are still missing. Source needed: 东北方言词典 / 东北方言概念词典, or CNKI papers on 东北官话 语气词. A Shanghai International Studies University paper on 嚎 was found but its page was behind a captcha.
老 + adjective + 了: confirmed only as 'degree adverb with strong subjective emotion' by a 2023 abstract. The example sentences come from my combination, not from an opened source.
得劲: Wiktionary labels it Central Plains / Jilu, not Northeastern, so it was not added as a Dongbei word.
苞米: widely known as Northeastern but the opened Wiktionary page gives no dialect label.
啥前儿 and 白话: only on the uncited vocabulary section of zh.wikipedia 东北官话.
r- → y or l or zero by sub-region and age: the statements are uncited. Check 中国语言地图集 or a phonetic study.
No opened source compares Heilongjiang, Jilin and Liaoning at the province level.
Whether Dalian and Dandong belong to Jiaoliao Mandarin: the claim came from a search snippet only.
confidence_note: low-to-medium (vocabulary and set phrases: medium; grammar: low; phonology: low-to-medium, many source statements are uncited)
